newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: World's biggest miner RTZ-CRA sees 1996 profits drop.
newsitem.headline: World's biggest miner RTZ-CRA sees 1996 profits drop.

text.p: The world's biggest mining company RTZ-CRA on Thursday reported a 24 percent drop in 1996 profits following sharply lower metal prices and problems with its U.S. copper smelter.
Adverse exchange rates were an additional factor behind the profit fall to US$1.096 billion in 1996 from US$1.441 billion in 1995. The results were as industry analysts had expected.
But RTZ-CRA said its prospects remained good, adding it saw strong long-term growth in demand for metals and minerals.

"Whatever the short term fluctuation in market prices, we believe the group will be a beneficiary of the strong growth in demand for our products which is in prospect over the years ahead," RTZ chairman Robert Wilson said in a statement accompanying the group's results.

Prices for RTZ-CRA's main metals, copper and aluminium, fell respectively 22 and 16 percent in 1996. The company was also dogged by delays in the production build-up at its flagship Kennecott smelter in Utah in the United States.
But Wilson said action was taken to address the smelter problems and added that "substantial improvement will become evident during 1997".
RTZ-CRA said it will benefit in 1997 from the first full year of production at the Greens Creek silver, zinc and copper mine in the United States.
Expansion of the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand and increased operations at the huge Escondida copper mine in Chile will also have a positive impact, said the world's biggest miner.
